  • “What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

It has been revealed that brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick remarked. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick remarked. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a massive game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

According to recent reports, “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

Sources indicate that at the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

It has been revealed that mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

It has been revealed that and after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react swiftly enough.

Recent findings suggest that pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

In a recent development, brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

Sources indicate that “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

It has been revealed that for Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he stated. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y.

The situation is what it is, but we’ve got to be a little bit careful of the exposure and how we jump on that.

Sources indicate that the start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a significant way.

There’s a number of things we’ll look at, we’ll dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong. We can’t accept that as a group. I take responsibility, the performance towards the second half that’s on me. We’ll have to get better, we have a significant game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to get back to winning football matches.

Sources indicate that we’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one. We didn’t find a way out of it. That’s up to me and the staff to help the players and guide them through it. I think we all know that in the end tonight feels like a major disappointment.

We’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.

We have to find the answers for Sunday.

Bruno Fernandes has provided an enhancement on his contract situation with Manchester United, as AC Milan watch on closely.

It has been revealed that during an interview with Sky Sports, Fernandes admitted that Manchester United have offered him a upcoming deal, with his current one expiring at the end of the season. However, he has put the talks on hold as he wants to see what their ambitions are.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, sky add that the Portuguese playmaker has rejected two contract offers from United. The Red Devils’ initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began, but it was turned down. United do have a one-year option that they can trigger.

“No, there’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘he’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United,” he noted.

“I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester! Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always demonstrated how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

Industry observers note that “I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club indicates, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.

“Yes, the club offered me a fresh contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay. And as you stated, there are no negotiations going on.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most notable thing now is that the club gets back to win games.

Sources indicate that “My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am. I will never hide from that, I will never say, no, our position at the moment needs to be to get top four.”.

Recently, Fernandes’ name has been mentioned in conjunction with Milan, who are looking to boost the level of their squad with quality signings. The former Sporting CP man knows head coach Ruben Amorim well, and could help fill the void if Luka Modric retires/departs.

Fabrizio Romano even spoke of the idea being ‘more than a dream’ for the Rossoneri management, while The Athletic also reported that the 32-year-old is an option Milan are exploring after he turned down United’s second offer.

Since joining Manchester United in January 2020, Bruno Fernandes has recorded 113 goals and 111 assists in 340 appearances across all competitions.

Birmingham City returned to winning ways on Wednesday night as they beat lowly Burnley 2-0 at Turf Moor. Chris Davies‘ side won their fifth away game of the season; only West Brom have picked up more points on the road this season.

Once again, August Priske and Jay Stansfield were key to BCFC’s victory. The attacking duo combined again on Wednesday night, with Stansfield setting up Priske for the side’s opener. Between them, they have scored and created 15 goals for Birmingham City, and Davies will expect more of the same on Saturday.

In a recent development, bolton Wanderers meanwhile are starting to get a little repetitive, showing spells of competing at Championship level before finding a way to lose. It was exactly the same on Wednesday as Steven Schumacher‘s side lost 3-1 to West Brom. The Trotters fought back after chasing the game, but just as they took control, they conceded twice, leaving the same old feeling at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

For Schumacher, his concerns include poor home form and a failure to convert chances, but the clear glitch is in defence. BWFC have conceded 33 goals this season, conceding three in each of their last three games, and only the Championship’s bottom two have conceded more.

Industry observers note that “Birmingham City are clicking at the right time. There’s a lot of pressure on Chris Davies to deliver and aside from the loss to Stoke City, it is exactly what they are doing. Beating Burnley on Wednesday was routine for this group of players, and this game should be too.

It has been revealed that “Bolton Wanderers have shown they can compete, but down the stretch, they just don’t have the quality. The Trotters need to head to St Andrew’s and set up to be hard to beat, or they could face a really long afternoon in the Second City.

According to recent reports, “On form and quality alone, there’s only one winner in this game. For me, that is BCFC.”.

“Birmingham City produced an ideal response to their Stoke City defeat by beating Burnley in midweek. The Clarets might have been a favourable matchup for the Blues, but they got the job done in a professional manner to keep pace with the three Championship sides above them.

In a recent development, “Professional is a good way to describe BCFC’s season so far. Unlike last season, they’ve not got bogged down after negative results. All three times Chris Davies’ side have lost this campaign, they’ve responded with a victory in their next game, highlighting their strong mentality.

“Bolton Wanderers have shown they’re dangerous this season, but they are beatable. Steven Schumacher’s men come into games to impose their will and they are capable of doing that, but I think a problem is that Schumacher is still working out his best defence, and that is preventing them from finding success at the back – 33 goals conceded in 17 games indicates that.

Sources indicate that “You can’t write off Wanderers, but you have to think the Blues win here. I’m going for a home win.”.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:27 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 23 November 2026.

Arsenal will be keeping everything crossed ahead of goalkeeper David Raya undergoing tests on what appeared to be a shoulder or arm injury sustained against Newcastle.

The Gunners' No1 went off in the second half in the 2-2 draw at St James' Park, supporting his arm or shoulder before he was replaced by back-up Kepa Arrizabalaga.

It leaves everyone associated with Arsenal nervous, as they face potentially a sustained period of time without a key part of their impressive defence.

Raya appeared to pick up the injury by running into Newcastle's Will Osula after claiming the ball from a cross.

As he attempted to run forward to start an attack, he collided with the striker and hit the ground in pain.

After a brief period of treatment on the field, he was substituted, supporting his arm, and replaced in the game.

"I'm petrified!" Ian Wright and Jamie Redknapp on why David Raya coming off injured vs Newcastle is a massive worry for Arsenal 🧤 pic.twitter.com/F5uAgjFdp0.

Arsenal face a nervy wait to find out the extent of David Raya's injury picked up against Newcastle on Saturday.

Manager Mikel Arteta has been left sweating at the idea of being without his No1 for a busy Christmas period.

'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news,' Arteta said: 'He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know.

'It was a knock, I don't know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow.

It has been revealed that 'We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.'.

The Gunners will play nine more games before the end of the year as they look to push forward in both the league and Champions League.

Hull reignite genuine survival hopes with late Oli McBurnie double to down Brighton, as talk of Seagulls emulating Leicester City-style fairytale is made to look foolish

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.
  • It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:08 EST, 23 November 2026.

When Brighton owner Tony Bloom was asked about his club’s title prospects last week, he suggested they could emulate Leicester City’s 2015-16 fairytale and win the Premier League.

It was a bold claim, yet Fabian Hurzeler’s men looked anything but title aspirants after being downed by Oli McBurnie’s dramatic late double for newly-promoted Hull City.

Brighton have been the most credible challengers to Arsenal so far this season. That cannot be denied.

With Manchester City wobbling alarmingly, and the rest of the traditional big guns largely off the title pace, the Seagulls have at least given Mikel Arteta’s champions something to think about.

But this bitterly cold afternoon in East Yorkshire was a reality check for Hurzeler’s men and a harsh lesson in taking the chances that come your way.

Brighton didn’t and McBurnie most certainly did, firing home clinically from close range twice in added time shortly after Joao Costinha had been sent off.

Oli McBurnie scored a late brace to secure a brilliant three points for Hull against Brighton.

McBurnie has made a habit of leaving it late – the rejuvenated Scotland striker struck a 95th-minute winner in the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough at Wembley in May.

Hull had gone eight Premier League games without a win before Brighton’s visit and this success lifted them to 11th.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic noted of McBurnie: 'I’ve never had any doubts over a ‘Braveheart’ like Oli because he’s a natural leader and very vital for us.'.

Asked where the setback left Brighton’s title hopes, Hurzeler said: 'We don’t focus on the table – we focus on performances and how we can make the right improvements into the team.

Industry observers note that 'That’s the same if we had won or lost, but today showed there are still things we need to do better. That’s what we will do and then see what the outcome will be.'.

Brighton arrived as favourites and could have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the table.

Hull were indebted to a remarkable display from their Greek goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who reduced Brighton to an afternoon of frustration and futility.

The visitors had 10 attempts at goal during the first half alone, forcing Hull’s summer signing into a string of fine saves and also being denied by the woodwork.

At times the Seagulls’ pretty patterns threatened to cut the Tigers apart as the likes of Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and the effervescent Pascal Gross – on his 300th appearance for the club – knitted them together superbly.

Georginio Rutter was involved in a move which saw De Cuyper cross low from the left flank to the onrushing Gomez, whose close-range effort was superbly saved by Tzolakis.

That set the tone for an outstanding display by the 24-year-old Greece international, who arrived in the summer from Olympiacos as part of the newly-promoted Tigers’ £150million spending spree which saw 18 players signed.

Hull lacked nothing in spirit and fight but Brighton had the quality and constantly threatened to open up their hosts.

As half-time approached, Rutter saw a close-range shot repelled by Tzolakis after Yasin Ayari’s effort rebounded off the crossbar.

The Tigers were constantly grateful to their goalkeeper, who made another save to keep out an effort from Gomez on the stroke of half-time.

Tzolakis continued to prove unbeatable in the second half too, and his opposite number Bart Verbruggen was left grateful to the woodwork after a cross-shot from substitute Sorba Thomas hit the crossbar.

Mohamed Belloumi was also a lingering threat for Hull on the right flank and he should have scored after cutting infield before firing wastefully wide.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (right) produced a remarkable display to keep Brighton out.

As the game wore on, there was an inescapable feeling that Brighton could be punished for their wastefulness as Hull showed the kind of courage which deserves, and usually gets, its rewards.

Regan Slater cleared a shot from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line before Brighton lost Joao Costinha to a second yellow card with a minute remaining.

The Tigers sensed blood, pouring forward to lead in the first minute of added time as McBurnie expertly sidefooted them in front from Lucas Gourna-Douath’s neat pass to cap a delightful flowing move.

It has been revealed that moments before the final whistle, Hull struck again as McBurnie swept home from close range again from Mo Belloumi’s assist. Cue delirium in the home stands.

McBurnie took the acclaim but Tzolakis was Hull’s star man as Jakirovic acknowledged: 'Tzolakis was amazing and we could have been two or three-nil down without his saves.

'We stayed alive because of him and then won the game at the end. Ciao!'.

Hull had failed to win since beating Manchester United and Coventry in their opening two games in August.

Hull reignited their survival hopes with a precious win against an in-form team.

Crucially, however, they have been competitive in every game this season and are now unbeaten in six home matches.

Can they survive? 'Of course, and every win is so important,' declared Jakirovic.

'I wish this feeling I have now would never stop but I know how demanding this league is.'.

Hurzeler could certainly attest to that.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4091 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

According to recent reports, so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a substantial career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

In a recent development, what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

In a recent development, chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Recent findings suggest that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

It has been revealed that allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has noted supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

In a recent development, cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

It has been revealed that all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

Industry observers note that with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

According to recent reports, FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

In a recent development, A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Industry observers note that mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

According to recent reports, lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Recent findings suggest that substantial cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

It has been revealed that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

It has been revealed that what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

According to recent reports, maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

Recent findings suggest that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

According to recent reports, credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

Sources indicate that as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

It has been revealed that A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

According to recent reports, he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic indicates some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

According to recent reports, kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Industry observers note that khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

It has been revealed that as Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a fresh five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

Industry observers note that 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

According to recent reports, keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

Sources indicate that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Sources indicate that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Industry observers note that philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Recent findings suggest that milan’s mission upon the resumption of Serie D was a quite simple one: to build on the three wins in a row and put some pressure on ChievoVerona at the top, a side that they beat away from home a few weeks ago. They faced a Tritium side who started the day second bottom, with just two wins so far.

Sources indicate that it could hardly have been a better start for the Rossoneri, as they took the lead after less than 13 minutes. Levin Asanji was the player who got it to keep his great form going, finishing with an audacious but wonderfully-executed back-heel flick from a cross to the near post by Emanuele Borsani.

A sweeping counter-attack saw Asanji run in behind, and he unselfishly squared to Lorenzo Ossola who slotted past the goalkeeper to double the advantage.

  • The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026.

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'.

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr.

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child.

It has been revealed that 'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most key thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more key in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'.

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

Olympiacos vs AC Milan - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:04.
  • Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium.
  • Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:04.

Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium.

Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.

Milan will head into the second half of the league phase with a point to prove, having lost three out of four games to date - including the last two without scoring.

Recently beaten by Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, Ruben Amorim's side have failed to even find the scoresheet since Goncalo Ramos struck in their lone win against Red Bull Salzburg.

A paltry tally of three points leaves the Italian heavyweights in real danger of being knocked out, as they sit 28th in the Europa League table and only the top 24 will go through.

By contrast with their continental results, Milan are showing clear signs of progress in Serie A, where they occupy fourth place, just ahead of city rivals and reigning champions Inter.

The Rossoneri have taken 15 points from the last available 18 - while scoring at least twice on each occasion - and they have only lost one domestic fixture this term.

Aiming to keep pace in the Scudetto race, Amorim's men hosted surprise high-flyers Frosinone last weekend, when they eventually cruised to a 5-1 win, with rising star Alphadjo Cisse scoring again.

However, Milan must now head to Greece, where they memorably won the 1994 Champions League final but have never beaten native hosts in six prior attempts.

In particular, Milan's two previous visits to Piraeus ended with a 2-2 draw in 1959 and a 3-1 defeat in 2018, when Olympiacos won the most recent meeting.

That was also in the Europa League, and the Greek giants presently sit sixth in this season's league phase - seven points clear of the Rossoneri.

As things stand, Olympiacos will directly enter the last 16, despite losing their perfect record last time out.

Across all competitions, they had won nine straight games before being held to a 0-0 draw by Rennes, which followed victories over Jagiellonia Bialystok, Marseille and Sparta Prague.

All told, Imanol Alguacil's side have lost just one of their last 18 fixtures, and Sunday's 6-2 destruction of 10-man Iraklis left them second in the Greek Super League standings.

Furthermore, Olympiacos have only suffered one defeat in their last 13 Europa League matches - while keeping nine clean sheets - so they will surely fear no-one on home turf.

Olympiacos form (all competitions):.

AC Milan form (all competitions):.

Amorim has typically shuffled his lineup for Europa League games - albeit not to positive effect - and several fringe players should feature for Milan.

Omari Hutchinson and Ardon Jashari have often played, while Cisse could start again; the new Italy international already has six Serie A goals and he scored a hat-trick away to Salzburg earlier in the campaign.

At the other end of the spectrum, experienced captain Mike Maignan can return after serving a one-match ban for his red card against Bournemouth.

Goncalo Ramos is set to overcome a minor calf problem, but the visitors must travel without Mattia Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek due to injury.

Meanwhile, Olympiacos are missing long-term absentees Ayoub El Kaabi and Yusuf Yazici, plus South American pair Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze.

Leon Bailey bagged two goals and an assist at the weekend, so he could link up with Armando Gonzalez, who is the hosts' top Europa League scorer with two.

Portuguese playmaker Jota Silva has racked up the most shots in this season's league phase; however, just two of those 17 attempts have found the target and none have hit the net.

Olympiacos possible starting lineup:.

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

AC Milan possible starting lineup:.

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Rabiot, Cisse; Ramos.

Milan may have struggled to score in Europe, but with Amorim developing an exciting front line, they average above two goals per game in Serie A and are overdue to convert some chances.

That stated, Olympiacos are a formidable force on home soil, so they can keep their unbeaten streak going with a hard-fought draw.

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

It has been revealed that one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

It has been revealed that “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Recent findings suggest that asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel remarked. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel mentioned. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

Industry observers note that “It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

It has been revealed that “So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

Tuchel stated that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

In a recent development, “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

According to recent reports, “It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Major Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches.

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season.

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

Recent findings suggest that so why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic major boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the problems we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

Industry observers note that city had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Recent findings suggest that iraola is aware of all this and remarked on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City.

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month.

Industry observers note that ‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

Sources indicate that ‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a massive game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’.

According to recent reports, asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’.

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Industry observers note that against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

It has been revealed that to take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's massive boys.

In a recent development, and that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their latest manager in a few weeks.’.

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

According to recent reports, but Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the substantial boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I mentioned at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’.

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Substantial Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

It has been revealed that but a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

Unai Emery has made four changes to his starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League fixture against Galatasaray.

With the condition of the RAMS Park preventing Villa from training on the surface on Monday, it felt plausible that Emery could protect some of his star players.

Instead, barring the exclusion of Pau Torres and Emiliano Buendia, the Spaniard has arguably named the strongest lineup from the options available to him.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis has moved over to right-back to replace Aaron Wan-Bissaka, with Tyrone Mings getting the nod over Torres in the middle.

Joao Gomes has returned to the midfield in place of Leon Goretzka, while John McGinn returns ahead of Buendia.

Nicolas Jackson has retained his place down the middle of the attack, with former Besiktas frontman Tammy Abraham among the substitutes.

Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho has again been left out of the Villa squad.

Meanwhile, Okan Buruk has recalled the likes of former Tottenham Hotspur defender Davinson Sanchez and ex-Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder Mario Lemina to his Galatasaray XI.

Former Arsenal man Lucas Torreira is another ex-Premier League player to be selected in the team.

However, former Norwich City star Gabriel Sara has dropped down to the substitutes' bench, joining Leroy Sane.

Lesley Ugochukwu - on loan from Burnley - is also kept in reserve, but top goalscorer Victor Osimhen remains sidelined through injury.

Galatasaray XI: Ugurcan; Singo, Sanchez, Bardakci, Jakobs; Torreira, Lemina, Elmali; Akgun, Batrakov, Yilmaz.

Subs: Bitshiabu, Sara, Gul, Gundogan, Guvenc, Lus, Nhaga, Sane, Ugochukwu, Yilmaz.

Aston Villa XI: Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Mings, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson.

Subs: Bizot, Wright, Barkley, Buendia, Torres, Abraham, Mbaye, Bogarde, Goretzka, Wan-Bissaka, Hemmings.

#131013. Senegal champions again, but Morocco’s phone call allegation could open a latest legal fight

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (738 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Senegal champions again, but Morocco’s phone call allegation could open a latest legal fight

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 16:33.
  • Recent findings suggest that senegal have been officially restored as champions of Africa.
  • According to recent reports, it is a dramatic twist in a case that had poisoned African football since January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 16:33.

Recent findings suggest that senegal have been officially restored as champions of Africa. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) delivered its verdict on Tuesday 24 November and sided with the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), overturning the decision by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) that had awarded the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations to Morocco on a technicality. The Lions keep the title they won on the pitch in Rabat.

According to recent reports, it is a dramatic twist in a case that had poisoned African football since January. By cancelling the CAF appeal board’s decision of 17 March 2026, CAS sided with the Senegalese federation. The original result of the final is therefore restored: a 1-0 win for Senegal after extra time.

Recent findings suggest that the Lausanne-based court rejected the regulatory reading that had led CAF to penalise the Lions with a forfeit. It found that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, used by CAF’s appeal committee, were not applicable in this case, and that only the restart of play authorised by the final’s referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, counted.

Sources indicate that ‘By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,’ the court mentioned. ‘In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the “field of play” doctrine.’.

The doctrine gives priority to decisions made on the pitch unless there is evidence that the rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith. CAS said Articles 82 and 84 were only meant to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s behaviour leads the referee to declare that play has definitively stopped, and so did not apply. ‘In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law,’ the court added.

It has been revealed that the panel acknowledged that the referee had to decide in a climate of extreme tension, but mentioned that did not make the decision arbitrary and that his judgement did not appear to have been affected by factors outside the game. On the disciplinary side, it recalled that the FSF, coach Pape Thiaw and some players had already been sanctioned by CAF in separate disciplinary proceedings. The FSF appeal was therefore upheld, and the decision was unanimous.

On 18 January 2026, Senegal beat Morocco in the final thanks to an extra-time goal from Pape Gueye. Before that goal, the match had turned in stoppage time when referee Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty after a VAR intervention. Furious, coach Thiaw told his players to leave the pitch. After an interruption of around 16 minutes, the Senegalese returned, led by Sadio Mane. Brahim Diaz then missed the Moroccan penalty before Gueye decided the final.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) immediately contested the match. After its first complaint was rejected by the disciplinary committee, CAF’s appeal board declared Morocco the winners and Senegal forfeited on 17 March, applying Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations. The FSF went to CAS on 25 March, and a closed-door hearing took place on 8 October.

The ruling restores Senegal’s status as African champions, giving them a second AFCON after their 2022 triumph in Cameroon. The team, now coached by Patrick Vieira, has two continental titles.

For Morocco, the verdict is a heavy blow. The host nation, which hoped to win a second crown 50 years after its first in 1976, sees the pitch result confirmed and remains credited with one title. But the case may not have said its last word.

A few hours before the verdict, the FRMF reported an ‘incident’. According to RMC, the federation denounces an alleged telephone conversation on Sunday between Ulrich Haas, one of the judges appointed to the case, and Abdoulaye Fall, president of the FSF. If proven, that contact could be a flaw Morocco might exploit before the Swiss Federal Tribunal, which can review CAS decisions on procedural grounds.

It has been revealed that for its part, CAS notes it received no report from Morocco. It remains to be seen whether the controversy marks the start of a latest legal saga.
